plan.title: Connect a fail-closed Linux synthetic status reader guard

criteria.description: Reader guard protocol tests reject unexpected TGIDs, overflow, malformed/short events, monitor EOF/read/write failures and closed guards; event descriptors close on failure. Existing descriptor/mapping checks fail closed when unavailable or occupied. The collector services the guard throughout child lifetime, rejects terminal failures and cleans up its direct child on timeout/error.

Synthetic measurement offers explicit Linux-only reader guarding, binds successful rows to the prepared manifest and guard protocol, rejects unavailable guard setup without summary, and preserves warm/first-run and cold-cache refusal behavior.
Existing actual status smoke and prepared-workload provenance remain passing.

limitations: E03b-2 only. Guarding is opt-in, requires Linux fanotify permission events and complete procfs visibility in an approved isolated environment. It rejects observed pre-existing workload/binary file descriptors and mappings, but is not a hostile same-user/root sandbox or proof against unobserved races. Privileged native Linux integration is exercised separately; portable mocked protocol cases do not establish kernel support. Guarded launch includes a shell handoff in elapsed time and waited-child peak RSS. No reset, mincore/start ordering, cold-cache enablement, performance threshold, new dependency or installation. Implementation may exceed 300 lines to keep event parsing, procfs preconditions, collector lifetime and failure tests in one rollback boundary.
